Scientists, cyber technologists, and psychics all belong to the collective known as The Alpha. Using a uniquely sentient A.I. to calculate any possible outcome, they hope to govern all people with a system of perfect control.

The Tech subfaction focuses on applied science and R&D to facilitate colonization of the Astrox system. Many members utilize cybernetic modifications to better interface with the ancient sentient program that regulates their activities.

The Civil subfaction has representatives in areas of programming, entertainment, subspace communication, diplomacy and other more clandestine activities. Members include a wide range of celebrities, agents, Alpha-sanctioned program directors, and artists.

The Trade Barons concern themselves with economics first, and everything else a distant second. Profit and enterprise are the driving forces of civilization and the common bond that classifies this faction.

The Financial subfaction regulates markets, establishes banking institutions, and sets interest rates. Members are an elite group of bankers and those with enough wealth to buy a seat at one of the meetings.
The Commerce subfaction is a loose conglomerate of entrepreneurs and big business chains moving personnel and goods around the system. Members count their worth in cargo space and units sold.

No subfaction could be more diverse than The Pirate Syndicates. Gangs of hardened frontiersmen banding together to live by their own rules. Taking whatever they can and smuggling bliss funds their appetite for more advanced ships.

There is nothing so human as independence, and the Outlaws are defined as a group by their unwillingness to be part of a group. Living on the fringes of other communities, they survive on their own merit for most everything, and "borrow" the rest.

The Sovereign are isolationists and independents who simply want to survive without interference. Living with bare essentials in the most remote areas, they thrive through ingenuity and salvaging. Due to their nomadic existence, most are considered derelicts at worst and space gypsies at best.

The Temple of the Void subscribes a spiritual destiny to the event horizon at the center of the Astrox universe. Believing the void beyond the stars to be a great divine barrier that must be surpassed for humanity's ascension into the heavens.

The Missionary subfaction consists of spiritual advisors servicing the people of Astrox. Members are more concerned with easing the suffering of the inhabitants and providing care for recovering bliss addicts than unraveling the secrets of the void.

The Temple Orthodox and it's clergy devote themselves with study and prayer centered on worshiping the Void. They believe that by embracing the nothing, they will free themselves from the Astrox universe and attain enlightenment.

The Labor faction is one of the largest in Astrox. Made up of artisans and trades workers, both skilled and unskilled, they provide the necessary material for development and expansion. Mining, production, and service all fall under the Labor faction.

The Contractors Union is responsible for the planning, implementation and building of all new products or structures. From the lowly cook to the esteemed warp engineer, manufacturing and production would not exist without careful planning from The Contractors Union.

The Extractors mine the various asteroids and refine the derivative ores to produce goods and materials used for construction. Members work long shifts in dangerous conditions and often live their entire lifetime on a remote dig site.

The Law regulates all other factions through the universal laws drafted by the first settlers. Responsible for modifying and enforcing the laws, it is made up of people who like structure and a clear chain of command. Private security contractors commissioned by law agencies also fall into this faction.

As the name implies, this militarized faction maintains cutting edge combat ready ships to provide security and police the Astrox universe. Often criticized for the aggressiveness of thier pilots, it is still the first to respond when an outpost is overrun with pirates.

The Judicial subfaction is the foundation of the Law faction itself. Ratifying all laws to oversee everything from building and trade contracts, Sovereign relocation programs, and public domain disputes. The Judicial body is notably complicated and oftentimes resolutions to cases occur long after all participants have died.
Adamyte Ore
Very common construction materials can be extracted from Adamyte. Its abundance makes for easy mining and it is always in high demand. Very high compression allows for easy storage in the cargo bay.
Gradeon Ore

This soft mineral is often used in agriculture and medicine. Gradeon is very resistant to bacterial growth, and is often referred to as the 'Sterile Stone'. When refined, Gradeon produces many of the basic building blocks needed to sustain human life.
Quazor Ore

High prized for its incredible strength, Quazor is used in the manufacturing of ship components such as armor and hull structures. Average demands have remained stable for this resource, securing it's place on the market.
Lokken Ore

Lokken is a soft ore that serves as an excellent electrical conduit. Used in consumer goods, high end computer systems and often found in jewellery. When refined, Lokken becomes an essential part of any construction project.
Torim Ore

This uncommon ore is scarce throughout the region. Its high demand is due to its ability to store magnetic data. When refined, the Torim ore can produce vital constuction materials used in the maintenance and fabrication of ship components.
Plasite Ore

A rare ore, sought after for its explosive properties. Used almost exclusively in the manufacturing of weapons ordinance and ammunition. Highly valued on commercial markets, as well as underground black markets.
Dynex Ore

An extremely rare crystal like mineral, prized for its beauty. In raw form, this ore can be dangerous due to its ability to store radiation for long periods of time. Highly valued and easily traded, Dynex is worth every cubic meter of your cargo bay.
Belasite Ore

Belasite is an extremely rare asteroid to find. It is very dense, and difficult to mine. This is mainly due to the extreme pressures caused by the collapsing of a nearby micro star. These rocks can fetch a great rate, and are prized for their utility.
Xenox Ore

Xenox is a very rare, and somewhat dangerous asteroid to harvest. They are very unstable and can easily explode if mined to rapidly with inferior equipment. Regardless of the danger, their value keeps the miners coming back for more.
Zai Ore

This is one elusive asteroid to harvest. They can form out of nowhere, only to fall apart moments later. If you are able to locate, and mine these rocks, a small fortune will be waiting at your nearest market.

Water
Water is a basic material used in construction of life support system components, and widely used in the process of fabricating other components.
Carbon

Carbon is a non-metallic chemical element that is widely used in construction and fabrication of more advanced crafting components. This material is in high demand and can easily be found in most common resources.
Oxygen
Used mainly in the construction of advanced life support systems, Oxygen is easy to find and profitable to refine. This base material is used in smelting and refining raw ore.
Salt Crystal
Salt Crystals are a valuable construction material that is used in almost all manufacturing processes. Salt helps to retain moisture and reduce the waste water produced by life support systems.
Hydrogen

Hydrogen is a gaseous element that can easily be classified as the most abundant element found in the Astrox universe. Although it can be found everywhere, it remains in high demand, and will fetch a decent price at any market.
Magnetic Quartz
Magnetic Quartz has a large number of applications. This material has extreme magnetic properties that are used in research and electronics. Highly values with a constant demand.
Calcium

Calcium is formed on the surfaces of a number of ores when moisture collects in the cracks of the asteroid. It is a reactive metal that forms a dark oxide-nitride layer when exposed to oxygen, and the radiation from a nearby microstar.
Plastix Strands
Plastix Strand is one of the strongest, most lightweight materials in the entire universe. Refined from Lokken asteroid ore.
Silicon
Silicon is a hard and brittle crystalline solid with a light metallic shine. It has moderate semiconductor properties and is commonly used in the manufacturing of cryo-pod systems.
Iron Coring
Iron Coring is a strong heavy metal often used in smelting and the construction of stations. Commonly found in Torim.
Nitrogen

Nitrogen has an extremely strong bond, that makes this raw material very important in manufacturing of start ships and structure. Abundant and easy to mine, nitrogen is a very profitable element for the average aspiring miner.
Oil

This viscous material is mainly used as a precursor to fuel production for star ships. Oil is also a great lubricant, and therefore remains in high demand by the labor faction. Oil prices fluctuate frequently, but almost always return a decent profit.
Copperi Cubex

A soft, pliable metal fragment found in a variety of ores. Used to alter the molecular properties of metal and considered extremely valuable by most fabricators. It also has some electronic applications as it is a great conductor of electricity.
Ceramic
Ceramic materials are brittle, hard, strong in compression, weak in shearing and tension. Used as an insulator in electronic devices, as well as various medical applications.
Acidic Residue
Acidic residues are acids left over from various chemical reactions. The exact acids left behind depend on the ingredients invovled in the reaction.
Aluminium Shard

Aluminium is a silvery-white, lightweight material, that is soft and easily malleable. Aluminium is used in a huge variety of products and manufacturing processes. Moderately valuable and easily harvested.
Bio Carbon
Bio Carbon is produced when carbon molecules are oxidized on the surfaces of some ores. Not altogether abundant, it is always in high demand, and produces moderate profits when harvesting.
Dynex Crystal

Dynex Crystals, often called Dynex Diamond, can store small amounts or radioactive energy inside the folds of the crystal. Very rare and very valuable, Dynex is often used in advanced fabrication and is highly traded on the markets.
Neutron Pods

These strange growths are a bi-product of refining more moisture rich asteroids. Neutron Pods are used mainly as a catalyst during the fabrication of high density metals. Originally discarded and thought to be useless, now quite valuable on the markets.
Steelium
Steelium is a very strong and durable base material used mainly in the construction of star ship armor. Once refined, Steelium can fetch a decent market price and is easily traded on the markets.
Calciate Residue

Calciate Residue is formed on Belasite or Xenox ore when micro meteros strike the surface of the rock, causing tiny explosions that leave Calciate deposits. These deposits are used in fabrication and manufacturing.
Titanyte

Titanyte is a larger base material with a considerable weight to mass ratio. This material is a stabilizing mineral used in refining metals. Titanyte can deliver huge returns for any miner luck enough to find it.
Silveryte
Silveryte Powder is a highly explosive material used mainly in the manufacturing of weapon ammunitions. This base material can be somewhat tricky to collect and refine, but retains a very high value.
Goldyte
Goldyte Dust has special properties that reflect and refract light with little signal loss. Usually found in the more remote regions of the Astrox universe.
Prometheum
Prometheum is a very strange base material, that can change it's molecular structure base on the ambient vibrations of the region it is found in. Extremly valuable and highly profitable.
Uranium
Uranium is a very valuable base material, prized for its radioactive properties and used mainly by the Science faction. Easily traded on the markets but quite difficult to refine.
Nuts And Bolts

A general assortment of various bolts and nuts used in fabrication of larger more complicated components. In high demand in most labor regions, as the fabrication of modules and star ships require large numbers of these bolts.
Fasteners
Fasteners are everyday items used to make non-permanent joints in everything from shelving to welding frames. Cheap and easy to find but always in high demand.
Steelium Beam
Steelium , the basis of all construction. Sturdy and resilient, This metal has become the building block of the Astrox universe.
Assorted Gaskets
A mechanical seal, often made of rubber or thin metal. Gaskets are meant to prevent leakage between joining parts to stop rusting and excessive wear.
Reinforced Rubber
Much like normal rubber but with a few special ingredients to help make an even stronger if less flexible material.
Lubricant
Lubricants are often based in oils or grease, used to keep moving components moving smoothly, cause the last thing you want in space is for your airlock to stick.
Steelium Pipes
Hollow Steelium pipes. When combined with valves and tanks they help make a sturdy and reliable fluid transfer system.
Metal Brackets

A simple and cheap industrial component that is used in the construction of just about everything and anything found in the Astrox universe. Used to fasten large parts together, Metal Brackets can be found in most production facilities.
Liquid Coolant

Liquid coolant is an industrial component used in manufacturing and fabrication. Used mainly to cool down engines and high powered energy cores. This resource is normally in high demand, and can produce decent profits for those who produce it.
Carbon Fiber
A special mesh made almost entirely of carbon. Noteworthy for such qualities as high tensile strength and chemical resistance while also being extremely lightweight.
Metal Gears
Metal Gears are used mainly in mechanical and insdustrial construction projects. It will be hard to find a module, station or ship that does not use gears in it's construction.
Metal Valve

Metal Valves are used to control the flow of liquids and in some cases, gases. Relatively easy to fabricate. These components are found in abundance throughout the Astrox universe, as they are usualy manufactured on an as needed basis.
Thermal Insulation
Equally useful in home and in ships, thermal insultaion will keep you from freezing or frying in the harsh depths of space.
Aluminium Rivets
Smooth cylindrical aluminum rods with a wider head at one end. Rivets are useful for making super strong joints or stapling on plates of armor
Rubber Tubing
Rubber tubing is used in the transfer of gases and fluids, as well as for hydraulic and pneumatic systems. Expect to need plenty of these when building anything of even moderate complexity.
Small Storage Tank

Storage tanks are used to store various types of materials and components in a larger, more industrial capacity. Liquids, gases, grains and smaller particles can be stored in these containers. Easy to fabricate and cheap to purchase.
Plastic Caps
A wide and varying assortment of caps and tops, useful for everything from electrical work to making sure your spray paint stays fresh.
Mechanical Belts
Rubber, metal, or specialty belts for joining rotating systems or mechanisms
Assorted Springs
Tightly coiled metal rods good for a wide range of uses.
Ball Bearings
These are used in just about everything that moves, and somethings that dont. Whatever your doing or making,youll likely need plenty of ball bearings to make it work.
Polymere
Polymers are a family of materials defined by the trait of macromolecularity. Featuring a wide range of properties due to the many different types, there's a polymer for just about any purpose.
Circuit Board
Made of thin conductive sheets pressed between non-conductive materials, and etched with electrical conduits and components

Thermal Sensor
A pack of heat sensitive materials and gadgets.
Mechanical Switch

Fiber Optic Cables
Long cables made of pure glass, cladded in special materials that refract light. Fiber optics use the refractive properties of glass and cladding to transmit information at literal light-speed.
Capacitors
Capacitors are electrical components that use electrical fields to store power.
Optical Interface
Touchscreens and other optical interfaces allow for clear and visualized control systems and communications.
Regulator

Battery Core
Battery cores are the central component to batteries and contain the power storing medium and its container.
LED Lights

Large Processor
A large processing unit capable of handling hefty but simple computing tasks.
Motion Sensor

Pressure Sensor
Devices for measuring changes in atmospheric or physical pressure.

Small Motor

Titanyte Plates
Titanyte plates make for top grade armor and paneling. Their strength and durability come at the cost of being difficult to manufacture.

Servo Controls

A liquid chemical compound added to other liquids to prevent the solidification and freezing.
Cleaning Chemicals
Floor polish and rust remover, Dish detergent and Hand sanitizer. If it exists, it will eventually need to be cleaned. That is where these cleaning chemicals come in
Colored Dye
Natural and artificial color dyes for clothing or other products.
Assembly Tools
Assembly tools are for putting together all those nuts and bolts and other pieces to make components. Very important to shipyards and Stations with fabricators.
Calibration Tools

For DIY specialists and mechanics alike. Crates containing an assortment of power tools and battery packs.
Medical Instruments
various devices used in medical treatment and surgical procedures. Space is dangerous, and medical supplies are always in high demand.
Personal Clothing

Communication Device
Transponders and connected datapads for medium and long distance communication.
Hygiene Products
Cleansers, soaps, and antibacterial products for healthy living in the crowded life of spacestations.
Transport Units
Containers for containing containers containing various substances and objects.
Foodservice Products
In these crates and boxes are stacks of trays, insulated containers and plethoras of forks and spoons. People do not only need food, they also need a way to eat it.
Office Supplies
It's a lot of work keeping track of all the trading and logistics of an entire station. Office supplies are an ever essential supply for keeping daily life on stations running smoothly.
Textile Fabrics
Squares of cloth and wool for common clothes. Though not worth as much as the clothing they make, textile fabrics are in continuous demand and will be worth your while in bulk.

Food synthesizers, refrigeration units, and even the kitchen sink. This equipment is bulky and heavy, but is also worth a tidy sum.
Office Furniture
Sofas, chairs, beds and more. Everything needed to make a home or office a little cozier.

Old fashioned stoves, ovens and microwaves for those who want more natural food and cooking, just like great-great-great-great grandma used to make.
Interior Lighting
Bulbs and fixtures for lighting up the infinitely dark void.
Entertainment Electronics
Tvs and vidya games, nothing here is essential,but everyone needs to relax sometimes. These are sure to bring a smile to somebody's face.

Media Recordings

Musical Instruments

These carefully packed containers hold synth wood reproductions of instruments like guitars and pianos. In the silence of deep space people will pay good money to hear anything other than the grinding of gears and hum of ventilation.
Sporting Equipment

Childrens Toys

I guess I can tell you what little I know. Everyone has their own theory about what happened. There are even a few drinking games based on the most popular ones.[n][n] I have heard a few interesting stories when I was a kid. structure_recon_1.txt>60>How did he die?
structure_recon_1.txt>70>Really? You remember nothing at all?

He didn't die exactly. Well, not as far as anyone knows. He just kind of disappeared one day. He left for a salvage job, dropped off a payload, and that was it. No one ever saw him again. A few of his contractors came looking for him when he stopped bidding on new jobs, but that was it. He vanished.
structure_recon_1.txt>62>Maybe He found something better out there.

My uncle knew a lot about the imperium. He was part of a special salvage crew that would breach the deadspace barrier in search of artifacts and relics of the imperium ship. He was always pretty quiet about what he found out there, as per his contract.
structure_recon_1.txt>42>What is 'Deadspace' exactly?

Deadspace is the dangerous void you find if you travel too far from the center of the sector beacon. Each sector has an established gravitational field. It keeps the electromagnetic radiation from the void at bay. If you stray too far, you might find yourself on a one way trip to 'Never seen again' land. I have never been out there myself, but I have heard stories.
structure_recon_1.txt>44>Tell me more about the deadspace.

My uncle told me once, He ran into a younger version of himself out there. Same ship, same clothes. He was just younger. [n][n]Granted, He had been without food or water for almost a week before a missionary caravan happened to pick up his distress beacon. This was long before we had the fancy food synths and purifiers we have now. Anyway, you have to take it with a grain of salt. An ex blisshead suffering from starvation and delirium? who knows what he saw.
structure_recon_1.txt>46>That would be crazy if it were true.

Yeah, I would have to agree.  He kinda changed after that. I onced asked him if he spoke to his younger self. He replied, 'I warned him.' He never told me of what,  I suspected it was important by the grin he had on his face at the time. My uncle was something else.
structure_recon_1.txt>48>So he never shared any info about the imperium?

Welcome to Astrox new friend! I know you are still a bit disoriented, but that will pass. I have been assigned to help you learn some of the basics. You can always find me at any of the stations here in Void Starcross. Drag this window around, if you need to, and you can leave it open as I help you along if you like.
tutorial_basics.txt>6>Tell me about the basic Interface.
tutorial_basics.txt>50>How do I fly this thing?
tutorial_basics.txt>60>I want to know more.

With the basics out of the way, take a moment to review a few more things before you head out to make your fortune. Life Support is a big deal, so you are going to need to learn how to stay alive out in space. Once you understand the basics, I suggest you do a little mining to get a feel for things. When you feel comfortable enough, accept a few scanner missions to help you earn your way to a new ship.
tutorial_basics.txt>15>What is this (Life Support Systems) ?
tutorial_basics.txt>30>Teach me about (Mining) for profit.
tutorial_basics.txt>40>What are (Contract Missions) ?

The Life Support System is the part of your ship that keeps you alive while you are moving around through space, You really have to be careful. You cannot expect to just fly around endlessly in that soupy mix of radiation, poison dust, random voltage spikes and who knows what else. Even though we have been floating around out here for a couple of hundred years, we still haven't seen it all. We do know this, without a well maintained Life Support System (LS), you will die, and that is a fact.
tutorial_basics.txt>20>Okay, so how does it work?

If you open your STATS PANEL ( Z key ), you will see a RED meter. That meter represents how much time you can spend out in space before you need to dock with a station. Each area or SECTOR of the Astrox universe has a unique environment. There are 4 main factors that make up this environment. How much light there is. How much water is available. What the temperature is, and lastly, how toxic the sector is. Your ship's Life Support System will help to balance things out so that you remain safe.
tutorial_basics.txt>22>Okay, I am starting to understand.

Your ship comes ready with a basic LS system installed. All you need to do is plug-in the support components that can be purchased at the station markets. We will start you off with one or two level 1 items. Some food, and a water filter. You can open your LIFE SUPPORT PANEL by pressing (K). Drag these items from your CARGO BAY (Tab), and drop them onto the LIFE SUPPORT PANEL.
tutorial_basics.txt>24>Got it.

As you upgrade the Life Support System, you will be able to endure more extreme environments. The time that you can remain undocked will increase, along with your range of exploration. Just remember, you need to leave yourself enough LS to make it back, or to the nearest station or else your journey will be a one way trip.
tutorial_basics.txt>10>Thank you for the great advice.

Mining is a great way to get started. Sure, you are not going to get rich overnight, but at least you can rely on a steady source of income. Mining is simple and there is not much risk involved, as long as you keep to the safe areas of Astrox. First, you are going to head over to the GARAGE. You can find these at most of the stations. Once inside, you can outfit you ship with a couple of mining lasers.
tutorial_basics.txt>32>Okay, what next?

You can also expand your cargo capacity using the Cargo Expanders. These are passive modules that allow your ship to carry more ore back to the station. Once your ship is ready to go, UNDOCK from the station and find the closest rock you can. There are a number of ways that you can target and select the rock, but I recommend just double clicking it. This will automatically engage the auto-pilot system and your ship will fly within range of the resource.
tutorial_basics.txt>34>Makes sense, then what?

Once your ship is within range, the auto-pilot computer will adjust the speed and keep your ship at a safe distance. By this time, you will want to fire up those mining beams so they can start collecting ore. With each cycle of the laser, ore will be extracted from the resource and placed into your cargo bay. Once you cargo bay is full, return to the nearest station so you can earn some Credits for your hard work.
tutorial_basics.txt>36>How do I sell the ore exactly?

Once you dock at the station, check to see if there is a MARKET. If there is no MARKET at this station, undock and look for a station that does. Once inside the MARKET, just open your CARGO BAY (Tab) and drag these items you wish to sell onto the MARKET.  You do not need to refine the ore prior to selling it. However, in some cases, the refined material can be worth more than the raw ore itself.
tutorial_basics.txt>10>Thanks for the advice.

Contract Missions are a great way to earn additional Credits while moving about the Astrox universe. There are a number of different types of missions, and these missions are posted for the public to bid on. If you see a mission you think is worth the effort, you can accept the job. Once the job is done, you are paid for your hard work and often rewarded with a skill point or two, as well as some experience.
tutorial_basics.txt>42>That sounds pretty easy.

Well, at first glance it may seem very simple, but you must keep in mind that if you fail to complete the mission due to time, or your inability to perform the assigned task, you will be responsible. This can be very costly and set you back a large sum of Credits. I recommend that you start with very simple missions. Nothing that requires a large deposit or a huge cargo bay.
tutorial_basics.txt>10>Thanks for the help.

The interface is pretty straight forward, most of it you will figure out fairly easily. You will notice that there are a number of small TRIANGLES poking out from the edge of the screen. These will give you access to various different panels that hold important information about where you are, what you are carrying, and what is around you. Let's take a look at your CARGO BAY. Press the (Tab) key to see what you currently have on board.
tutorial_basics.txt>7>Got it.

You can control your ship a few different ways. You can fly around using WASD, using shift for afterburners. You can also use autopilot (E key). This will automatically fly your ship to what ever target you have selected. You can double click an item to toggle on the autopilot, or click and hold over a target. This will open a small menu allowing you to select a few additional options.
tutorial_basics.txt>51>Okay, simple enough.
You can drag and drop items from your CARGO to the markets, the refinery, even out into space. You will drag and drop items to and from the GARAGE to install weapons and upgrades onto your ship.
tutorial_basics.txt>8>Sounds easy enough.

Most of the interface has tooltips. Take some time while you mine to explore some of the interface. It will not take long before you understand how things work. You can talk to just about everyone, and they can often tell you important things. Sometimes you get lucky and find someone with a wealth of information. Take your time and explore the safe areas like Void Starcross before venturing too far away.
tutorial_basics.txt>10>Okay.

You can use the middle mouse wheel to zoom the camera in and out. The left click button is used for selecting targets, the right click will rotate the camera around your ship. You can temporarily focus on your target by clicking and holding the mouse wheel button. If you zoom all the way in, you will activate the cockpit view. Zoom all the way out, and you will see the entire Astrox universe.

[s2][cyan]Basic Drones Tutorial (5 of 8)[/][/s][n]The range of your drones will depend of the size and quality of each individual drone. If this happens, the drone icon will be displayed as [orange]ORANGE[/] to indicate it is out of range.[n][n]The range of a drone will also affect how close it has to be to a target before it can perform its task. If the energy is depleted, the drone will crawl back to the ship, and wait for rescue and recharge.[n][n]Some drones will deliver cargo to your ship's [lime]CARGO BAY[/]. My name is Jacob, and I will be walking you through the basics of Mercs and how to get set up running your fleet. There are a few things you are going to need to know before you get started.[n][n]Say the word and I will begin your training.
tutorial_mercs.txt>100>Okay, teach me about Mercs.
tutorial_mercs.txt>200>Not right now.

[s2][cyan]Basic Mercs Tutorial (1 of 8)[/][/s][n]This first step we will need to cover, is training the [magenta]FLEET COMMAND[/] skill. For each level of this skill that you train, you will be able to control one additional Merc.  The maximum number of Mercs your are able to control in your fleet is 10.[n][n]You will need to find the [magenta]FLEET COMMAND[/] skill at one of the stations in your starting sector. Train this skill to level one when you are ready to proceed to the next step.
tutorial_mercs.txt>10>BACK
tutorial_mercs.txt>110>NEXT
No problem, I will be right here waiting when you change your mind. It's not a bad idea to take a refresher course from time to time.
tutorial_mercs.txt>0>Okay.

[s2][cyan]Basic Mercs Tutorial (2 of 8)[/][/s][n]Now that you have the [magenta]FLEET COMMAND[/] skill trained to level one, you are now able to hire a Mercenary from the[yellow]STATION  LOUNGE[/]. The [yellow]LOUNGE[/] will not only provide you a place to hire Mercs, but it will also provide you the much needed RnR that can be required to keep those space-faring ruffians happy and ready to work.[n][n]Head over to the [yellow]STATION LOUNGE[/] and let us take a look at the available mercenaries.
tutorial_mercs.txt>100>BACK
tutorial_mercs.txt>120>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Mercs Tutorial (3 of 8)[/][/s][n]Once inside the [yellow]LOUNGE[/], click the [yellow]MERCS[/] button for a list of all the available mercenaries at this station. Not every station will have a [yellow]LOUNGE[/], but all lounges will have Mercs for hire.[n][n]You will notice each merc has a different ship, modules, and faction rating requirements. Find a Merc that fits your style might take some time, so pay attention to their equipment, and their specialty.[n][n]A Merc's specialty will indicate what kind of work the Merc is prepared to do. Forcing your mining Mercs into combat is not recommended. Neither is making your combat Mercs mine ore. They will eventually tire of your chores and abandon the fleet.
tutorial_mercs.txt>110>BACK
tutorial_mercs.txt>130>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Mercs Tutorial (4 of 8)[/][/s][n]I recommend hiring a low level Mining Merc for your first addition to the fleet. By shopping around a few stations, you will find a Mining Merc that is suitable and not too expensive. Keep in mind, you will need to have some basic faction standing before you are able to hire any Merc of any faction. This can easily be achieved by running a few missions for that station. Each Merc will have the same faction as the station at which they reside.[n][n]Once you are ready to hire your first Merc, and you are sure that you meet all the faction and skill requirements, we can proceed to the next step.
tutorial_mercs.txt>120>BACK
tutorial_mercs.txt>140>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Mercs Tutorial (5 of 8)[/][/s][n]From the [yellow]LOUNGE[/] display list, [green]SELECT[/] and the [green]HIRE[/] a Merc. They will automatically be added to the fleet, and you will see their ship slide into dock formation with your ship.[n][n]You are now the commander of your very first, and very small fleet. Learning to control your fleet will not be a simple, but it will not take long at all before you understand how it all works.[n][n]When you are ready to continue with the lesson. [green]UNDOCK[/] from the station and we will continue this tutorial where we have some room to move around.
tutorial_mercs.txt>130>BACK
tutorial_mercs.txt>150>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Mercs Tutorial (6 of 8)[/][/s][n]We will need to open the [yellow]COMMAND PANEL[/] in the bottom right of your HUD. You can use the hotkey (F) to open the panel quickly. This panel will default to the [yellow]FLEET COMMAND[/], but it can also display all of the [yellow]DRONES[/] your ship is currently controlling. For now, we will focus only on the [yellow]FLEET[/] panel. [n][n]The [yellow] FLEET [/]panel will display all of the active Mercs you currently have flying with you in your fleet. These Mercs will stay with you at all times, and this panel will help you keep track of their behavior.[n][n]Take a moment to explore the options and functions of the [yellow]FLEET[/] panel. The mouse over text will describe each button's function. You can also select and deselect multiple Mercs, allow you to send commands to all the selected Mercs.
tutorial_mercs.txt>140>BACK
tutorial_mercs.txt>160>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Mercs Tutorial (7 of 8)[/][/s][n]By clicking the [yellow]MERC AVATAR[/] you can open up a individual [yellow]COMMAND PANEL[/] for only that particular Merc. From here, you are able to activate the Merc's [green]AutoTask[/].[n][n]Some Mercs have the ability to function all by themselves. They will not require any input until they are unable to perform their main [green]AutoTask[/] action, in which case they will return to you for instructions or assistance.[n][n]You have full control of how to command the Mercs, but you cannot outfit their ships with new equipment. If you want a better Merc with better gear, you will have to hire one.
tutorial_mercs.txt>150>BACK
tutorial_mercs.txt>170>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Mercs Tutorial (8 of 8)[/][/s][n]You can use the ship's onboard [yellow]TACTICAL SENSORS[/] [lime](SPACEBAR Key)[/] to easily see what Mercs have been selected,  This display will also make it easier to identify your ships on the map.[n][n]There is quite a lot to learn when it comes to Mercs, Why not take this old Merc Command Manual I have on backup file. You can read more about Mercs by opening your [yellow]JOURNAL[/] and reading through it. Mostly the stuff we just covered, but there are a few bits of good information to be gleened from it.
tutorial_mercs.txt>160>BACK
tutorial_mercs.txt>175>Thank you.
There you go. You can access this document any time you need to. Just open up your [yellow]Pilot's Journal[/] and you will find it under DOCUMENTS. Anyway, you take care out there. Stay safe.
doc_tutorial_mercs_1.txt
tutorial_mercs.txt>0>Thank you.

Well hey there, You must be the Newgee everyone is talking about. I am Adji, and I have been assigned to help you learn the basics of navigation.[r]It won't take long at all to grasp the basics, so just let me know when ever you are ready, and we can get started.
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>100>Okay, teach me the basics.
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>200>Maybe some other time.

[s2][cyan]Basic Navigation Tutorial (1 of 8)[/][/s][n]Before we get started, let's go ahead and [yellow]UNDOCK[/] from the station. You will find a button for that on the right hand side of the station under [yellow]STATION SERVICES[/].
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>10>BACK
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>110>NEXT
No problem, I will be right here waiting when you change your mind. It's not a bad idea to take a refresher course from time to time.
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>0>Okay.

[s2][cyan]Basic Navigation Tutorial (2 of 8)[/][/s][n]Now that we are outside of the station, rotate your [yellow]CAMERA[/] around using the [lime]RIGHT MOUSE CLICK[/] and [lime]DRAGGING[/] the mouse around until you see one of those big rocks floating around out there. The [lime]MOUSE WHEEL[/] can be used to [yellow]ZOOM[/] the [yellow]CAMERA[/] in and out.
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>100>BACK
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>120>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Navigation Tutorial (3 of 8)[/][/s][n][lime]LEFT MOUSE CLICK[/] on an item to lock onto the object. The object will appear in your ship's [yellow]TARGETING SYSTEM[/]. You can toggle the [yellow]TARGETING SYSTEM[/] using the [lime](T key)[/].[r]The [yellow]TARGETING SYSTEM[/] will display all of the current targets your ship has locked.
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>110>BACK
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>130>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Navigation Tutorial (4 of 8)[/][/s][n]By clicking any target from the list of targets in your [yellow]TARGETING SYSTEM[/], your ship will focus on that target, and additional information will be displayed on the  [yellow]HUD[/] about the selected target.[r]Now, let's take a look at our [yellow]AUTOPILOT[/] panel. You can toggle the [yellow]AUTOPILOT[/] panel by using the [lime](R Key)[/].
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>120>BACK
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>140>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Navigation Tutorial (5 of 8)[/][/s][n]Your ship can automatically autopilot to any target you have scanned. If your ship's [yellow]AUTOPILOT[/] is turned on, your ship will automatically travel to the target and stop once it gets within range.[r]Let's turn on your ship's [yellow]AUTOPILOT[/]. Press the [lime](E Key)[/] on the keyboard. You will notice that your ship will begin moving to the selected target.
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>130>BACK
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>150>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Navigation Tutorial (6 of 8)[/][/s][n]There are a few different ways that you can activate your ship's autopilot. [lime]DOUBLE LEFT CLICK[/] any target on the map to autopilot to that target.[r]You can toggle the [yellow]AUTOPILOT[/] by clicking the small [lime]AUTOPILOT TOGGLE[/] button located in the [yellow]AUTOPILOT[/] panel in the upper right of your display.
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>140>BACK
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>160>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Navigation Tutorial (7 of 8)[/][/s][n]You can manually fly your ship around using the [lime]WASD[/] keys on your keyboard. The [lime]SHIFT[/] key will activate your ship's [yellow]AFTERBURNERS[/].[r]Take a moment to fly around using the [lime]WASD[/] manual controls. You can use these controls in conjunction with the ship's [yellow]AUTOPILOT[/].
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>150>BACK
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>170>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Navigation Tutorial (8 of 8)[/][/s][n]You can use the ship's onboard [yellow]TACTICAL SENSORS[/] [lime](SPACEBAR Key)[/] to easily click on those small fast moving ships, or those tiny rocks off in the distance.[r]With a bit of practice, you will be zipping around out there in no time. If you ever need a refresher, you know where to find me.
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>170>BACK
tutorial_navigation_basics.txt>0>Thank you.

If you are interested in learning some information about how to orbit your ship around a target, I would be happy to help. Orbiting is simple, and it shouldn't take long for you to grasp the basics. So what do you say? Are you ready to start this short tutorial?
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>100>Sure, why not.
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>200>Not right now.

[s2][cyan]Ship Orbits Tutorial (1 of 6)[/][/s][n]It is possible to program your ship’s computer to use trajectory information to orbit any target you currently have scanned. Orbiting a target can have some benefits when it comes to combat and resource gathering. As the commander of your ship, you are given the ability to adjust a number of factors that will determine how the ship behaves when orbit parameters have been met.
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>10>BACK
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>110>NEXT
Sometimes it can be helpful to take a refresher course, just in case you missed something the first time.  I will be right here waiting if you change your mind.
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>0>I will keep that in mind.

[s2][cyan]Ship Orbits Tutorial (2 of 6)[/][/s][n]The orbit can be controlled by using a few options located on the AUTOPILOT panel. This panel will provide the 4 main areas that control the ship’s orbit. [n][n]The Orbit Toggle button that will allow you to enable and disable the ship orbit at any time. This is followed by the target distance option and the direction and angle controls. The last indicator controls the speed of the orbit.
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>100>BACK
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>120>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Ship Orbits Tutorial (3 of 6)[/][/s][n]The direction of the orbit can be controlled by setting the orbit angle to a positive value (clockwise orbit) or a negative value (counter clockwise). [n][n]If you want the ship to continue to face the target you are orbiting, use a small value like (-10, or 10). If you prefer more of a broadside orbit, use a larger value like (80 or -80).
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>110>BACK
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>130>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Ship Orbits Tutorial (4 of 6)[/][/s][n]The speed at which your ship will orbit the target may slightly change as the ship adjusts it’s turnspeed and lateral shift. This is done to maintain the target orbit distance you have set. Using a low speed orbit can be great for mining and salvaging operations. High speed orbits can prove beneficial during combat engagements.
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>120>BACK
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>140>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Ship Orbits Tutorial (5 of 6)[/][/s][n]The orbit distance will control how far away the ship should be from the center of the orbit. Setting the orbit distance to a low value will cause the ship to orbit closely to the target. This will cause the ship to move quickly around the object. [n][n]Setting the target distance to a high value will cause the ship to take more time to cycle the object, even though the ship is traveling at the same speed. Setting the target distance can be helpful in combat when trying to keep your ship at range from the enemy raiders.
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>130>BACK
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>150>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Ship Orbits Tutorial (6 of 6)[/][/s][n]You can use the orbit abilities of your ship to gain a favorable position on your enemy during combat. The station garage will allow you  to adjust the rotation of each module so that while in orbit, your weapons will have enough mobility to point at the target.How much rotation, and which direction to rotate will depend on how you set the angle of orbit. It may take a bit of trial and error to find the best configuration for your ship, but the benefits can prove rewarding.
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>140>BACK
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>160>NEXT

See there, that didn't take long at all. If you ever need a refresher course, stop by and I will run you through the basics again.I guess I could make it easy on you an give you a copy of this tutorial document. You want it?
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>175>Great, I will take it.
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>0>No thanks, I don't need it.
There you go. You can access this document any time you need to. Just open up your [yellow]Pilot's Journal[/] and you will find it under DOCUMENTS. Anyway, you take care out there. Stay safe.
doc_tutorial_ship_orbits_1.txt
tutorial_ship_orbits.txt>0>Thank you.

Wormholes are a strange phenomenon out here in the Astrox universe. We don't know everything there is to know, but over time, we have been able to piece together some of the basics.[n][n] This tutorial will walk you through some of those basics and help you to locate and survive the exploration of these wormholes.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>100>Okay, teach me about Wormholes.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>200>Not right now.

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (1 of 10)[/][/s][n]Wormholes are a rare anomaly in the Astrox Universe. They are natural warp gates to unseen sectors not shown on the map until explored. Wormholes use natural cosmic energy to warp a ship from one end of the wormhole to the other. The energy involved can take time to store up in the wormhole. When the wormhole is used, energy is used as well. This can cause the wormhole to become unstable and eventually collapse it entirely.[n][n]It is currently unknown what causes wormholes to generate, but we do know it has something to do with concentrated energy. Wormholes have a small gravitational pull, and often collect trash and debris from the sector. In some cases, the items can be extremely valuable.[n][n]Wormholes can be some of the most dangerous places in the universe. Hostile environments and extremely low security can prove deadly for even the most seasoned pilots.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>10>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>110>NEXT
No problem, I will be right here waiting when you change your mind. It's not a bad idea to take a refresher course from time to time.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>0>Okay.

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (2 of 10)[/][/s][n]Finding wormholes can be tricky, since they do not spawn very often. When they do, it is hard to know where they are. You cannot see them very well with the naked eye, but using some specialized equipment will help you locate their position. [n][n]This may seem confusing at first but do not worry you will quickly get the hang of it and be able to find yourself a paradise or Raider hole whenever you want.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>100>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>120>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (3 of 10)[/][/s][n]The [green]Active Scanner[/] will report if a Sector has Wormhole energy nearby. Just turn the Active Scanner on and wait for it to cycle, if nothing appears this means there currently isn't a Wormhole. If a report appears it will also provide the signal strength and will display the current relative distance (does not include direction) from your ship. [n][n]Pick a direction and move your ship approx. 100m and wait for it to cycle again, this will give you this distance again and using this information you can pilot towards the signal source.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>110>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>130>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (4 of 10)[/][/s][n]For example if the Wormhole shows at 1000m and you move 100m towards a station/structure/rock and on the next cycle it shows you are now 1100m you know the Wormhole is roughly the opposite direction of your current position. [n][n]Turn your Passive Scanner on (set to gate mode in the filter) and once you are within Passive Scanner range the Wormhole will become targeted.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>120>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>140>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (5 of 10)[/][/s][n]The sector area that a wormhole will transport you to will remain accessible even if the wormhole itself has collapsed. [n][n]Warp drive systems are still a viable way to travel to a wormhole sector, but they can be a nightmare if you find yourself without enough fuel to get back. This may require that you harvest a star for fuel, so it is highly recommended that you always carry a harvesting beam with you when warp driving to a wormhole. The wormhole sectors usually have  more jumps available at the exit gate, than the wormhole entrance.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>130>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>150>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (6 of 10)[/][/s][n]There are two different ways that you can keep a wormhole open and usable. The first way is to construct an energy generator near the wormhole gate. This will provide a source of energy to the wormhole and will constantly recharge the energy it uses to warp your ship. This will keep the wormhole open, however the number of consecutive uses is still limited. You will need to wait for the wormhole to recharge.[n][n]The second way to stabilize a wormhole is to construct a warpgate on top of it. Once a warpgate harness has been assembled around an entrance or exit, with a Energy Generator in range, the wormhole will transform into a warpgate, and no longer require an energy recharge for usage. If the warpgate is destroyed, the wormhole will collapse and the gate will no longer exist.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>140>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>160>Thank you.

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (7 of 10)[/][/s][n]Some wormholes have a stronger gravitational pull than others. These tend to collect crates from nearby battles and these crates can often contain valuable items. The crates will be scattered amongst the other garbage collected by the wormhole, so it may take some looking to find them. [n][n]Unlike normal crates, wormhole crates begin deteriorating even before they are unsealed for the first time. It is speculated that the warp process causes enough damage to break the seal in transit, as crates are not designed for traveling at worm speeds. Collect the crates before they expire, and their items are lost forever.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>150>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>170>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (8 of 10)[/][/s][n]It is not uncommon for Raiders to use the wormhole sectors as safe havens for their criminal activities. In many cases, the Raiders will set traps for unsuspecting wormhole explorers looking for easy profits from the mineral rich asteroids. These raider groups will hide cloaked in the asteroid fields and wait until you are mining before ambushing their unsuspecting victims. Always be prepared for combat when exploring wormholes, or you may find yourself caught off guard.[n][n]On rare occasions, Raiders will establish a hideout or headquarters inside a wormhole sector. If this is the case, you will know right away how dangerous the sector is. Raiders will be swarming around a centralised structure that usually houses the manufacturing of illegal Bliss. They will fight to the death to defend their operations, so tread lightly in these wormhole sectors.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>160>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>180>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (9 of 10)[/][/s][n]Although very rare, wormhole sectors can be quite pleasant from time to time. Moderate environments, resource rich, and not a single Raider in sight. These wormhole sectors make for  great mining operations, or even a full scale base with dozens of structures.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>170>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>190>NEXT

[s2][cyan]Basic Wormhole Tutorial (10 of 10)[/][/s][n]Well, that pretty much sums up what is known about wormholes at this time. I will go ahead and place this wormhole tutorial document in your [yellow]Pilot Journal.[/].[n][n] Be careful out there, as wormholes can be deadly to those low level inexperienced pilots looking for an easy score.
tutorial_wormholes.txt>180>BACK
tutorial_wormholes.txt>195>Thank you.
There you go. You can access this document any time you need to. Just open up your [yellow]Pilot's Journal[/] and you will find it under DOCUMENTS. Anyway, you take care out there. Stay safe.
doc_tutorial_wormholes_1.txt
tutorial_wormholes.txt>0>Thank you.

Basic Projectile Operation will provide you with all the basic knowledge about the operation, maintenance and upkeep of active module projectile weapons. The level of the Projectile module is directly linked to the level of operation required to use it.

This skill requires the Projectile Basic Operation skill trained to level 3.  Advanced Projectile systems not only provides pilots with additional training about the use of projectile weapons, but also unlocks the use of special projectile weapons. Each level of training provides a small bonus to all attributes dealing with projectile weapons.

This skill requires the Projectile Basic Operation skill trained to level 2.  This specialized skill will boost the effective range of all Projectile Weapons installed. Each additional level of this skill will further improve the range, with a maximum training level of 10.

This skill requires the Projectile Basic Operation skill trained to level 1.  Energy Optimization will reduce the energy requirements per cycle of each Projectile weapon installed. This can add up to a huge savings in energy during a simple 3 minute skirmish. Every skill level of training will further reduce the required energy to a max level of 10.

This skill requires the Projectile Advanced Systems skill trained to level 3.  The cycle time for every installed Projectile Weapon will be decreased with each training level of this skill. By reducing the cycle time, the rate of fire will increase and allow you to deliver additional rounds during those critical moments.

This skill requires the Projectile Advanced Systems skill trained to level 4.  This skill will provide pilots with specialized training that centers around maximum damage output for each installed Projectile weapon. 10 levels of focused training will provide any student with an advanced understanding of (AFDS) protocols. (Augmented Firepower Delivery Systems)

This skill requires the Projectile Advanced Systems skill trained to level 4.  An advanced mechanical course covering all areas of Projectile weapon operations in regards to durability. This skill teaches how to keep those Projectile modules running smooth with custom parts, mods, and in some cases, fabrication.
